reason: The text overwhelmingly portrays the Hebrews as a structured nation with collective identity rather than merely a family or religious followers. Key evidence includes: (1) explicit reference to 'twelve tribes of Israel' (שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל) demonstrating organized tribal/political structure; (2) the phrase 'kingdom of priests and holy nation' (מַמְלֶכֶת כֹּהֲנִים וְגוֹי קָדוֹשׁ) which explicitly designates them as a nation with political status; (3) repeated use of 'the people' (הָעָם) acting collectively with unified voice and agency; (4) appointment of elders and judges indicating national governance structures; (5) the people's collective responses and decision-making as a body politic. While genealogy (בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל - descendants of Israel) and covenant relationship with Yahweh are present, the text emphasizes their identity as an organized, covenanted nation with institutional structures that transcends mere familial or religious categories.
